subject: physiology
title: Leukocytes, Phagocytosis, and Innate versus Adaptive Immunity

steps.tx: White blood cells or leukocytes represent the mobile cellular defense system of the human organism, maintaining a normal peripheral concentration between four thousand and eleven thousand cells per microlitre. Produced in the bone marrow and lymphoid organs through **leucopoiesis**, leukocytes divide morphologically into granular granulocytes and non-granular agranulocytes.
steps.say: Leukocytes comprise the mobile defense system, numbering 4,000 to 11,000 per microlitre, produced through leucopoiesis and divided into granulocytes and agranulocytes.

rows: Histamine and heparin release in hypersensitivity

steps.tx: The frontline cellular responders to acute bacterial invasion are polymorphonuclear **neutrophils**, comprising sixty percent of circulating leukocytes. Characterized by segmented three-to-five-lobed nuclei and neutral-staining granules containing myeloperoxidase and lysozyme, neutrophils leave the circulation by diapedesis, migrating up chemical concentration gradients toward bacterial formyl peptides in directed chemotaxis.
steps.say: Neutrophils are the primary bacterial responders, possessing multilobed nuclei and microbicidal granules that migrate toward bacterial peptides via chemotaxis.

steps.tx: Internalisation of pathogenic microbes into intracellular phagosomes is termed **phagocytosis**. Opsonisation by immunoglobulin G and complement fragment C3b marks targets for rapid ingestion. Inside the phagolysosome, membrane-bound NADPH oxidase generates superoxide free radicals in a respiratory burst, while myeloperoxidase converts hydrogen peroxide and chloride into hypochlorous acid to destroy microbial pathogens.
steps.say: Phagocytosis ingests opsonised microbes into phagolysosomes, where NADPH oxidase generates a respiratory burst of superoxide and hypochlorous acid.

steps.tx: Eosinophils and basophils mediate specialized inflammatory responses. **Eosinophils** defend against large metazoan helminthic parasites by releasing major basic protein, eosinophil cationic protein, and histaminase. Basophils and tissue mast cells express high-affinity Fc-epsilon receptors for immunoglobulin E; allergen cross-linking triggers degranulation of preformed histamine, leukotrienes, and heparin, driving acute anaphylaxis.
steps.say: Eosinophils combat helminthic parasites with major basic protein, while basophils bind IgE to release histamine and heparin during allergic reactions.

steps.tx: Circulating monocytes migrate into tissues to differentiate into resident **tissue macrophages**, forming the reticuloendothelial system. Macrophages act as professional antigen-presenting cells, processing foreign proteins and presenting peptide fragments on major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II molecules to helper CD4-positive T lymphocytes, releasing interleukin-1 and tumor necrosis factor to orchestrate systemic fever and acute-phase responses.
steps.say: Monocytes mature into tissue macrophages, acting as antigen-presenting cells that display peptides on MHC class II to activate helper T cells.

steps.tx: Immunity divides into immediate antigen-independent innate mechanisms and delayed, antigen-specific **adaptive immunity**. Adaptive immunity relies upon lymphocytes: T lymphocytes mediate cellular immunity via cytotoxic CD8-positive cells and helper CD4-positive cells, whereas B lymphocytes differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells, providing humoral immunity and long-lived immunological memory.
steps.say: Adaptive immunity provides antigen-specific memory through T lymphocytes mediating cellular immunity and B-cell-derived plasma cells secreting antibodies.

left.title: Innate Immunity
points: No immunological memory upon repeated exposure

right.title: Adaptive Immunity
points: Robust long-lived memory with accelerated recall

steps.tx: Antibodies or immunoglobulins are Y-shaped glycoproteins consisting of two identical heavy chains and two identical light chains. The five major **immunoglobulin classes** serve specialized tasks: IgM serves as the pentameric primary response antibody, IgG is the abundant secondary monomer that crosses the placenta, IgA protects mucosal surfaces as a dimer, IgE binds mast cells, and IgD serves as a naïve B-cell receptor.
steps.say: Immunoglobulins divide into five classes: IgM for primary response, IgG crossing the placenta, dimeric secretory IgA, allergy-mediating IgE, and receptor IgD.

steps.tx: The humoral antimicrobial cascade in plasma is the **complement** system, activated through classical, lectin, or alternative pathways. All three pathways converge on C3 convertase, cleaving C3 into C3a and C3b. C3b functions as a potent opsonin, C3a and C5a act as inflammatory anaphylatoxins that recruit leukocytes, and terminal components C5b through C9 assemble the membrane attack complex to lyse target pathogens.
steps.say: The complement system converges on C3 cleavage. C3b opsonises bacteria, C3a and C5a recruit leukocytes, and the C5b-9 complex lyses microbial membranes.
